doc.title: Marshall Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 19, 2021

title: Stage mishaps and lost music
summary: A singer fell off a stage in Japan, and once the music was stuck on a train so the band played a whole gig from memory.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: I wanted to tell you that I watched a wonderful video this morning of a rather symphonic piece that started out with a harp and there was a big hole in the stage. And I was afraid you were going to fall in it.

You remember that set up? There was a hole in the stage on purpose it looked like and I was wondering is someone going to come out of that, but I kept thinking Marshall, please don’t fall in that thing.

We had the singer, the singer was in Japan singing, and he walked to the edge of the stage and disappeared. And what he had done, it was about five or ten feet, he fell down in the audience. And I turned around like this, I said, “Where’d the singer go?” And he was down in the audience and the people were gathering all around and the band kept playing. He disappeared and fell down off the stage, down on top of the people.
Well with all the performing that the band has done I’m sure there’s been some what we would call train wrecks you know, like no equipment, people getting lost, and —

Yeah, and then all the music got stuck on the train and we didn’t have no music now we have to play the gig without the music. So we played it. So it was a different gig because we had to play by memory everything. Ain’t but so much you can remember on Sun Ra’s tunes. You might remember the first introductions and the basic number but all the rest of the stuff in between you don’t know who or what, what, what, what. So we’d have to go on anyway. So we played all evening without one piece of music because the music got hung up on the train or something. You know it was late coming.

Was the role of the bass player different from an average band like Count Basie? You know like if that had happened to Count Basie group I would think many of the musicians would be keying in to where is the bass player going. That will help me to remember my part?
Yeah. You listen to the bass, yeah of course. Because each part — but when he changed you’ve got to change too. You see? So you’re listening to that and it’s not just one thing.
